summary: Rand's status report for the May 1971 meeting, answering RFC 116. It says software on the Rand IBM 360/65 was being updated for the new network protocol of RFC 107 and that a test logger was being built. No Telnet was planned until a specification was widely accepted.

plainLanguage.summary: Rand describes work on its network software and plans for a new computer. It also shares opinions about how the network group should organize its work.

subtitle: Rand's report on its network software, computing plans, and views of the Network Working Group.

tldr.problem: RFC 116 asked sites to report their status for the May Network Working Group meeting.
tldr.mechanism: Rand reports on changes to its 360/65 software, a test logger, planned services, and its views on the Network Working Group's role.
tldr.outcome: Rand planned to update its software for RFC 107, build an experimental logger, and later move services to a PDP-10. It also comments on working groups and long-term planning.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 131 as Unknown and records that it updates RFC 116. It is a report of Rand's plans and views in 1971.

sections.title: The 360/65 and PDP-10 Plans
sections.content:
Rand was changing its 360/65 software to follow the new NCP protocol in RFC 107, with completion planned before the end of May. It was also implementing a logger for experimental checks of remote-login procedures, which could send or receive EBCDIC, ASCII (8), or binary streams.

Rand planned to implement user and server TELNET after a specification was generally accepted, then move Network services to a PDP-10. The 360/65 connection would remain for a time, but no new programs were planned for it after September.
sections.plainLanguage: Rand was updating its older computer and building a tool to test remote login. It planned to move Network services to a PDP-10 later.

sections.title: Other Network Activities
sections.content:
The report says the UCSB/Rand Network activities had been described in RFC 113 and earlier in RFC 78. Rand's Climate Dynamics Project expected to use the facility more, and Rand had built a graphics program for displaying reduced UCSB data as graphs, contours, plots, and lists.

A working session on the Data Reconfiguration Service had been held, and Rand planned a paper about a Protocol Manager for experimental and production connection protocols.
sections.plainLanguage: Rand was also working with UCSB data and graphics. It planned to explore software that could support different connection protocols.

sections.title: Views on the Working Group
sections.content:
Rand supported the Network Working Group as a forum and favored small groups for particular specifications, provided interested contributors were not excluded. It worried about delays between forming a group and publishing its work, and suggested guidelines for timely reports.

Rand did not think the NWG should set the Network's long-term goals. It suggested that Principal Investigators discuss those goals and that the Technical Chairman report their views to the NWG.
sections.plainLanguage: Rand favored small teams for focused work, with open participation. It thought Principal Investigators should shape long-term goals and the NWG should turn them into tasks.
